world:wheel.title: The Wheel of Signs
world:wheel.summary: The twelve constellations that turn through the sky of Valdren over a year. Every child is born under one, and every people agrees the Sign shapes them before their town does.

sections.title: The Wheel
sections.text: Twelve star-signs turn across the night sky over the course of a year, one rising each month. Elves of [[culture:elf.starspire|Starspire]] charted them first, but every people knows them by name: the [[origin:anvil|Anvil]], the [[origin:lantern|Lantern]], the [[origin:comet|Comet]], the [[origin:fox|Fox]], the [[origin:oak|Oak]], the [[origin:bell|Bell]], the [[origin:tide|Tide]], the [[origin:hare|Hare]], the [[origin:wolf|Wolf]], the [[origin:hawk|Hawk]], the [[origin:ember|Ember]] and the [[origin:crown|Crown]].

sections.title: Where you come from
sections.text: In Valdren people say you come from your Sign before you come from your town. Every Sign has its folk-ways: the trades it favours, the gifts it gives, the habits its children share. Sign-houses in every big town feed and shelter travellers born under their star, which is why a hero far from home can always find their Sign's lamp in the window.

sections.title: The Pact and the Signs
sections.text: The [[faction:pact|Pact]] keeps a Sign-board beside every tavern board, and bands often look for heroes of Signs that fit together. A band with an Anvil, a Lantern and a Hawk is considered lucky everywhere.

quote: Tell me your Sign and I will tell you your trouble.

origin:anvil.title: Anvil
origin:anvil.summary: Born under the Anvil, the Sign of first winter: patient, sturdy and good with their hands. Anvils temper what they own and keep what they make.

sections.title: Folk-ways
sections.text: Anvil-born children are given a small hammer at their naming. Smiths, masons and shieldwrights are most often Anvils, and the Sign-houses of the Anvil are usually forges. Dwarves of [[culture:dwarf.ironhold|Ironhold]] consider it the luckiest Sign, and are not quiet about it.

quote: Strike while it is hot. Wait while it is not.

origin:lantern.title: Lantern
origin:lantern.summary: Born under the Lantern, the Sign of the longest night: kind, steady and quick to help. Lanterns are said to carry a spark of the Undying Light.

sections.title: Folk-ways
sections.text: The Lantern rises on Lantern Night, holiest night of the [[faith:lantern|Lantern Faith]]. Children born under it are thought blessed, and many become healers. A Lantern's first heal of any battle is said to land with the strength of the Light itself.

facts: Your first heal each battle is a crit
quote: Someone has to hold the lamp.

origin:comet.title: Comet
origin:comet.summary: Born under the Comet, the wandering Sign: brilliant, restless and impossible to predict. Comets do everything all at once.

sections.title: Folk-ways
sections.text: The Comet is the only Sign that moves across the Wheel instead of turning with it, and nobody can say exactly when it will rise. Comet-born children are famous for their tempers and their genius. In battle, their greatest blows set off chains of even greater ones.

facts: Late winter, never the same night twice
MEGA crits add 2 to the combo counter
quote: Brightest before it goes. Mind your eyebrows.

origin:fox.title: Fox
origin:fox.summary: Born under the Fox, the Sign of the thaw: clever, quick and never where you swung. Foxes turn every dodge into an opening.

sections.title: Folk-ways
sections.text: Fox-born children are told they were born laughing. They grow up into traders, scouts and thieves, and the [[faction:quiet-hand|Quiet Hand]] has a Fox lamp in every house. A Fox who slips a blow strikes back before the swing is finished.

facts: After a dodge, your next hit is a crit
quote: The fox is never caught in the trap. It is caught asking how the trap works.

origin:oak.title: Oak
origin:oak.summary: Born under the Oak, the Sign of spring rain: tough, rooted and hard to knock down. Oaks start every fight a little shielded.

sections.title: Folk-ways
sections.text: The Oak is sacred to [[faith:green|the Green]]. Oak-born children plant a tree at their naming and are said to grow as it grows. Farmers, wardens and soldiers love the Oak, and an Oak in the band means someone will still be standing at the end.

facts: Start every pack with a small shield
quote: Bend if you must. Do not break.

origin:bell.title: Bell
origin:bell.summary: Born under the Bell, the Sign of the muster: loud, bold and impossible to ignore. Bells call the danger to themselves.

sections.title: Folk-ways
sections.text: The Bell is the Sign of the muster bells of the [[faction:pact|Pact]]. Bell-born children are loud from birth and grow into heralds, captains and the kind of tank who wants every enemy looking at them. Their taunts come back faster than anyone else's.

quote: Look at me. No, at me.

origin:tide.title: Tide
origin:tide.summary: Born under the Tide, the Sign of midsummer: calm, deep and patient. Tides flow back between every storm.

sections.title: Folk-ways
sections.text: The Tide rises over the sea at midsummer, and Freeport sailors swear by it. Tide-born children are calm, thoughtful and hard to anger. Their strength comes back between fights the way the tide comes in, and mages and priests born under it never seem to run dry.

origin:hare.title: Hare
origin:hare.summary: Born under the Hare, the Sign of high summer: fast, light and always ready to go again. Hares catch their breath before anyone else.

sections.title: Folk-ways
sections.text: Hare-born children are runners, messengers and dancers. Sandstrider runners of the dunes are nearly all Hares. Between fights, a Hare's energy springs back as if they had slept a whole night.

origin:wolf.title: Wolf
origin:wolf.summary: Born under the Wolf, the Sign of late summer: fierce, loyal and slow to cool. A Wolf's fury does not fade between fights.

sections.title: Folk-ways
sections.text: The Wolf is the orc Sign, sacred to the [[culture:orc.bloodfang|Bloodfang]] who ride wolves into battle. Wolf-born children are fierce and loyal to their pack. Their rage carries from one fight into the next, like a pack that does not stop running.

quote: Run with the pack. Bite for the pack.

origin:hawk.title: Hawk
origin:hawk.kicker: The Sign of the first strike
origin:hawk.summary: Born under the Hawk, the Sign of the harvest: sharp-eyed, precise and deadly on the first blow. Hawks open every boss fight with a crit.

sections.title: Folk-ways
sections.text: Hawk-born children see far and shoot straight. Elves of [[culture:elf.silverwood|Silverwood]] love the Hawk, and the [[faction:wayfarers|Wayfarers]] keep a Hawk lamp at every lodge. A Hawk's first strike on any great foe never misses its mark.

facts: Your first hit on each boss is a crit

origin:ember.title: Ember
origin:ember.summary: Born under the Ember, the Sign of the autumn fires: hot-blooded, bright and dangerous. Embers set their spells burning.

sections.title: Folk-ways
sections.text: The Ember is the draka Sign, sacred to the [[faith:ember-songs|ember-songs]]. Ember-born children are passionate and quick-tempered, and many become mages. Their spells carry a little of the [[world:underflame|Underflame]], and set what they hit alight.

facts: Spell crits set the target burning

origin:crown.title: Crown
origin:crown.summary: Born under the Crown, the Sign of the year's end: proud, generous and born to lead. The gifts of a Crown last longer.

sections.title: Folk-ways
sections.text: The Crown closes the Wheel each year. Kings of Aster were said to be born under it, whether they were or not. Crown-born children are leaders, organisers and inspirers, and the blessings they give their band linger longer than anyone else's.

facts: Buffs you give last 2 seconds longer
quote: A crown is a promise to everyone else.
